title: GST for service businesses in India
description: Which GST rate applies to services, when to charge IGST versus CGST plus SGST, and what every tax invoice must contain.
html:
Short answer: most services in India attract 18% GST; charge IGST on inter-state supply and CGST + SGST within one state.

Which GST rate applies?

Most services fall under 18% GST. Export-related services may be 0% (export of services).

IGST vs CGST+SGST

Inter-state = IGST; intra-state = CGST + SGST.

Invoice requirements

GSTIN of both parties, SAC code, place of supply, and tax breakup are mandatory. Try our GST Invoice Generator.

title: SEO basics every startup needs
description: The handful of search-engine fundamentals a new site needs before any paid growth: crawlable pages, clear titles, useful content and a sitemap.
html:
Short answer: make every important page crawlable, give it one clear topic, a unique title and description, and publish content that answers the question a customer actually types.

1. Make pages crawlable

Search engines and AI assistants read your HTML first. Pages that only appear after heavy JavaScript can be missed, so make sure key content is present in the page source.

2. One topic per page

Give each page a unique title and meta description that say what the page is, in plain words, and a single H1 that matches.

3. Answer real questions

Lead with the direct answer, then add detail. Pricing, timelines and comparisons are what buyers search for.

4. Ship the basics

Publish a sitemap, a robots file, fast mobile pages, and register the site in Google Search Console so you can see what is indexed.

title: Mobile app vs web app trade-offs
description: When a web app is enough, when you need a native or cross-platform mobile app, and how cost, speed and reach compare.
html:
Short answer: start with a web app if you need reach and speed to market; build a mobile app when you depend on device features, push notifications or repeat daily use.

Web app

One codebase, no app-store review, instantly updatable, and discoverable through search. Best for validating an idea, dashboards, marketplaces and internal tools.

Mobile app

Better access to the camera, location, offline use and push notifications, and a home-screen presence. A cross-platform framework such as React Native can cover iOS and Android from one codebase.

How to decide

If users come from search or links, begin on the web. If your product is used daily or needs the device hardware, plan for mobile. Many products launch web first and add a mobile app once usage is proven.

title: Measuring AI automation ROI
description: A simple way to estimate payback on an AI or workflow-automation project: hours saved, error reduction, run cost and build cost.
html:
Short answer: ROI = (value of time and errors saved per month − monthly run cost) ÷ build cost. Payback is build cost divided by the monthly net saving.

1. Measure the manual baseline

Count how many times the task happens each month, how long it takes, and the loaded hourly cost of the person doing it.

2. Estimate the saving

Multiply hours saved by hourly cost. Add the cost of errors, rework and delays that the automation removes.

3. Subtract running costs

Include model or API usage, hosting and a little maintenance time each month.

4. Compare with the build cost

Divide the build cost by the monthly net saving to get the payback period. Prefer processes that are frequent, rule-based and high volume.

title: API and backend development cost in India (2026)
description: A REST API starts at ₹30,000 and a GraphQL API at ₹40,000 on StackFox, with authentication, queues, caching and integrations priced individually.
html:
Short answer: a REST API starts at ₹30,000 (about 5-10 days) and a GraphQL API at ₹40,000. Individual backend features such as authentication (₹18,000) or caching (₹12,000) are priced separately.

APIs and data

  • Email & SMS Service Integration — from ₹12,000 per integration, about 2-3 days

REST or GraphQL?

REST is simpler and a good default. GraphQL helps when many different clients need different slices of the same data.

What changes the price

  • Endpoints and data models: more resources mean more build and tests.
  • Integrations: every third-party API has its own quirks.
  • Real-time and background work: queues, webhooks and sockets add moving parts.

FAQ

Do I need microservices?

Rarely at the start. A well-structured single service is faster to build and cheaper to run; microservices (₹60,000) pay off with large teams and scale.

title: How to write a software project brief (with a checklist)
description: A clear brief gets you accurate quotes. Cover the goal, users, must-have features, constraints and success measures, then use the free brief generator.
html:
Short answer: a good brief says what problem you are solving, for whom, what must be included in version one, and what success looks like. One page is enough.

The brief checklist

  • Goal: the business problem in one or two sentences.
  • Users: who will use it and what they need to do.
  • Must-have features: what version one cannot launch without.
  • Nice-to-haves: what can wait.
  • Integrations: payments, CRM, WhatsApp, existing systems.
  • Constraints: budget range, deadline, compliance needs.
  • Success measure: the number that tells you it worked.

Why it lowers your cost

Vague briefs produce wide quotes and mid-project changes. A clear brief lets each feature be priced on its own, which is how the StackFox catalogue works.

Do it faster

Use the free AI brief generator to turn a rough idea into a structured brief, then price it in the Build & Price tool.

FAQ

Should I include a budget?

Yes, a range. It helps the team recommend the right scope.

Do I need technical details?

No. Describe outcomes; the team can choose the technology. Our glossary explains common terms.

title: Freelancer vs agency vs service platform: how to choose in India
description: Compare hiring a freelancer, an agency or a priced-service platform like StackFox on cost clarity, accountability, speed and risk.
html:
Short answer: a freelancer suits small, well-defined tasks; an agency suits large, open-ended work; a priced-service platform suits buyers who want to see the cost of each piece before committing. The right choice depends on how clear your scope is.

Freelancer

  • Good for: small fixes, one-off pages, a single skill.
  • Watch for: single point of failure, limited range of skills, you manage the project.

Agency

  • Good for: large projects needing design, engineering and project management together.
  • Watch for: custom quotes that take meetings to produce, and scope-change fees.

Priced-service platform (like StackFox)

  • Good for: buyers who want line-by-line prices, a modular scope and a clear delivery estimate.
  • How StackFox works: every service shows its price and timeline, you build a cart, and payments are milestone-based with a client dashboard to track progress.
  • Watch for: unusual needs that are not in the catalogue; ask for a custom quote.

Questions to ask any provider

  • What exactly is included, and what costs extra?
  • How many revision rounds are included?
  • How are payments split across milestones?
  • Who owns the code and accounts at handover?
  • How do I track progress?
